one_line: A 6-second YouTube Short that is one unchanging infographic: a three-column table of 7 things parents say, what the child hears, and what to say instead.

hook.visual: Static image on black: a bright yellow headline banner over a table whose columns are yellow, red and green. The whole table is readable from the first frame.
hook.on_screen_text: 7 Things You Should Never Say To Your Children (7 דברים שאסור להגיד לילדים; original is English)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Inferred: a 'never say' headline plus a red 'They hear' column makes a parent check whether they say these lines. Everything is visible at 0.0s, so there is no build-up to wait through, and the colour split reads as wrong (red) vs right (green) at a glance.

beats.observed: Frame 0.0s already shows the full composition: yellow banner, three-column table (yellow We say / red They hear / green Say it this way), and a small yellow-on-black watermark below the table.
beats.spoken: No usable speech. Transcript is only the marker [Music].
beats.on_screen_text: 7 Things You Should Never Say To Your Children; column heads: We say / They hear / Say it this way; watermark PSYCHMASTERY-HD

beats.observed: Frames 1.0s to 3.0s are visually identical to 0.0s. No zoom, no highlight, no row-by-row reveal. Rows 1 to 3 are the top of the table.
beats.on_screen_text: Rows 1-3. We say: Can't you go faster? / Careful, you will fall! / Stop whining! Stop laughing!  They hear: You are not important to me. / The world is dangerous. Doing nothing is better. / Do not express your emotions!  Say it this way: We have only 10 minutes. / Take care of yourself. / You're probably tired, aren't you?

beats.observed: Same unchanged frame. Rows 4 to 7 sit in the lower half; text is small (about the size of a caption on a phone screen).
beats.on_screen_text: Rows 4-7. We say: How many times do I have to say it? / What have you done?! / You're doing it wrong, let me do it! / He does it so much better than you.  They hear: You're a loser! / You're a terrible child! / You are stupid! / You're worse than others.  Say it this way: You can handle it. I can help. Let's do it together. / I know you didn't meant to do it, but be careful next time. / Let me show you a trick for how to do it quicker. / I love you just the way you are.

beats.observed: Frame 5.0s is still identical; clip ends at 6.0s with no end card, no CTA text and no change.

payoff: The full list of 7 scripts is on screen from 0.0s and never changes, so the payoff is immediate. Reading all 21 cells in 6 seconds is hard, so the real payoff is likely a pause, replay or screenshot (inferred).
cta: None in the video. The caption (generic dark-psychology boilerplate that does not mention children) asks viewers to like, share, subscribe and comment "Unlock my mind!".
share_or_comment_trigger: Inferred: a parent sees their own phrase in the 'We say' column and either feels caught or sends it to a partner. The green column gives a replacement script worth saving. Comments are low relative to likes (2,000 comments vs 91,258 likes), so saving or sharing fits better than debate.
why_it_worked: Observed: the whole payoff (3 columns, 7 rows) is in frame 0.0s, so no viewer can drop before the value appears. Outlier 391.7x on an account median of 17,500 views.
Inferred: the we say / they hear / say it this way structure turns vague advice into 7 copyable sentences. A 1.33% like rate (91,258 likes on 6.85M views) is strong for a Short.
Inferred: 6 seconds is short enough to replay or loop. The caption is about dark psychology, not kids, so reach probably came from the image and title, not the caption (unverified).
paid_signal: no: like_rate_pct 1.33 is well above the 0.3 level that suggests paid promotion, and nothing in the frames looks like an ad.

solo_route.how: 1) Pick 5 to 7 everyday parent sentences that suit LumeBook's audience (bedtime, getting dressed, mess, sibling fights) and write each as Hebrew 'מה אמרנו / מה הילד שומע / איך אפשר להגיד'. 2) In Canva, 9:16 (1080x1920): LumeBook headline banner on top, a 3-column table laid out right to left in Hebrew, LumeBook colours instead of red/yellow/green if desired, max about 7 words per cell, font large enough to read on a phone. 3) Option: animate it so one row appears per second instead of a static image, which fixes the original's unreadable 6-second wall. Export as a 7 to 10 second video, and also as a 7-slide carousel for Instagram. 4) Put the LumeBook handle where the original has its watermark and end with one still of a LumeBook book page. About 1 to 2 hours of design after the wording is settled. Do not re-post the original: the origin of the graphic is unknown.
solo_route.needs: Because the original gives parenting advice with no named source or expert, LumeBook's version needs a cited source (for example a named paediatric or child-psychology guideline) or a barter expert who checks every 'They hear' claim before it is posted. Nothing else.

lumebook_version.hook_he: 7 משפטים שאנחנו אומרים לילדים, ומה הם שומעים
lumebook_version.concept: A Hebrew three-column 'we say / the child hears / say it this way' graphic, revealed row by row, with each replacement line checked by an expert or tied to a cited source. Last card shows a LumeBook page where the child is the hero, as a soft brand tie-in.

evidence_notes: Observed: all six frames (0.0s to 5.0s) show the same still image, so this is a static graphic shown as video. Text is crisp and consistent, with no visual sign of generated-image artefacts, but I cannot tell whether the table was designed in a template tool, made by an image generator, or taken from elsewhere. It has a small English slip in the last row of the Say it this way column ("didn't meant"). The burned-in watermark reads PSYCHMASTERY-HD, which matches the account name Psych Mastery, so the account branded it; who made the table is unclear. meta.json ai_made_how says slideshow and ai_tools is empty, so I name no tool. Spoken: the transcript is only [Music] across 6 s, so there is no usable speech transcript and no narration. I cannot describe the song. Inferred: the caption is unrelated boilerplate about manipulation and mind control, which mismatches the video; found_via says it was found by a YouTube search for 'things never to say to your child', which shows the video matches that search term, not why viewers watched. No expert, study or source is named anywhere in the frames or caption for the claims about what children 'hear'. Frame text is small, so I opened the 3.0s frame at full size to read the cells.
